item.title: Mazda Familia Rotary Coupe (1968)
item.description:
Publication: Car Graphic
Format: Road Test
Date: September 1968
Author: “C/G Test Group” (uncredited)

Road-testing the Mazda Familia Rotary Coupe

Summary: Car Graphic purchased the Mazda Familia Rotary Coupe as soon as it was released, and immediately began our customary long-term practical testing. Our magazine has already purchased the Toyota Corolla, Bluebird 1300, Lotus Europa, and Nissan Laurel one after the other, and is conducting controlled tests from a strictly objective standpoint while also putting them to use in daily life. The Familia Rotary Coupe is our fifth attempt to evaluate a new model through this method of long-term practical testing.

item.title: Mazda Familia Rotary SS (1969)
item.description:
Publication: Car Graphic
Format: Road Impression
Date: September 1969
Author: Masaru Mino

Road-testing the Mazda Familia Rotary SS

The Familia Rotary SS is a demonstration of the confidence Toyo Kogyo has in its aim of bringing the rotary engine into widespread everyday use. C/G has evaluated the rotary engine as a whole on several occasions and rated it highly.

The engine in the Rotary SS (and in the lower-priced E-type version of the Rotary Coupe announced at the same time) is the same 2-rotor, 982cc, 100ps unit used in the Rotary Coupe, which has now been on the market for a year, installed here in the Familia 4-door sedan. The engine and its ancillaries are exactly the same, but the manufacturer currently offers a choice of 2-barrel and 4-barrel Solex-Stromberg carburetors at the same price. With the 2-barrel type, maximum torque falls slightly from 13.5kgm/3500rpm to 12.8kgm/3500rpm, but the test car was fitted with the same 4-barrel type as the Rotary Coupe.

item.title: Mazda Familia Rotary SS (1969)
item.description:
Publication: Motor Fan
Format: Test Drive Report
Date: September 1969
Author: Atsuro Sasaki

Rotary SS: Charging Along the Tomei and Through the Mountain Roads

The Familia Rotary SS is the third model to be introduced in Toyo Kogyo’s rotary series, following the Cosmo and the Rotary Coupe. The smooth, high-performance character unique to the rotary engine has already been amply demonstrated in those two earlier models. We approached this test drive with great anticipation, eager to discover whether the Familia Rotary SS would live up to its growing reputation…
